SFPUC Employee Retirement Recognition for 25+ Years of Service
items.text: SFPUC Employee Retirement Recognition for 25+ Years of Service Dennis Herrera, General Manager, San Francisco Public Utilities Commission, introduced and recognized four SFPUC employees for their incredible service and dedication to the SFPUC for over 25 years of service: Mr. Terrence “Terry” O’Sullivan, Utility Specialist – Power Enterprise, was recognized for over 38 years of service with distinction. Ms. Glorina “Glo” Crisostomo, Chief Water Service Inspector – Customer Service Bureau, was recognized for over 37 years of exemplary service since January 1989

items.title: CONSENT CALENDAR
Approve Amendment No. 2 to Contract No. PRO.0113, Electric Billing Software as a Service Agreement, with Enterprise Solutions Consulting LLC
items.text: Approve Amendment No. 2 to Contract No. PRO.0113, Electric Billing Software as a Service Agreement, with Enterprise Solutions Consulting LLC, increasing the contract amount by $1,437,000, and increasing the contract duration by two years and six months, for a total not-to-exceed contract amount of $7,061,527 and a total contract duration of ten years to continue providing electric billing software, hosting, and as-needed technical services for the Oracle Custom electric billing system

items.title: Award Contract No. WW-668, Upper Yosemite Creek Daylighting Project, to Bauman Landscape and Construction Inc., to construct green infrastructure and restore right of way and public access areas within and adjacent to McLaren Park in San Francisco
items.text: Award Contract No. WW-668, Upper Yosemite Creek Daylighting Project, to the responsible bidder submitting the lowest responsive bid, Bauman Landscape and Construction Inc., in the amount of $15,265,175, and with a duration of 880 consecutive calendar days, to construct green infrastructure and restore right of way and public access areas within and adjacent to McLaren Park in San Francisco

items.title: Approve increase to the existing duration contingency for Contract No. WW-747, Seacliff Avenue Pump Station & Force Main Upgrade and Seacliff 1 Pump Station Demolition, with Minerva Construction, Inc.
items.text: Approve an increase of 248 calendar days to the existing duration contingency for Contract No. WW-747, Seacliff Avenue Pump Station & Force Main Upgrade and Seacliff 1 Pump Station Demolition, with Minerva Construction, Inc., for a revised duration limit of 864 consecutive calendar days (approximately two years and four months), with no change to the contract amount, to allow for additional time required for pre-packaged pump station procurement, electrical panel procurement, and coordination with Pacific Gas & Electric Company

items.title: Authorize the issuance of bonds (1) to fund the remaining development costs for 525 Golden Gate Avenue, and (2) to refund SFPUC’s outstanding BABs with proceeds of Revenue Bonds
items.text: Authorize the issuance of bonds or other forms of indebtedness (1) to fund the remaining development costs for 525 Golden Gate Avenue, the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC) headquarters building, in an amount of up to $731 million by prepaying outstanding 2009 City and County of San Francisco Certificates of Participation, Series D, executed and delivered as Build America Bonds (BABs) and (2) to refund SFPUC’s outstanding BABs with proceeds of Revenue Bonds or other debt obligations (including Commercial Paper Notes) of the Water, Wastewater, and Power Enterprises, as applicable, issued in an aggregate principal amount up to $493 million, $225 million, and $13 million, respectively; authorize the General Manager to enter into one or more bond purchase contracts with Barclays Capital Inc., or Barclays Bank PLC (Barclays), subject to the limits on compensation set forth in the resolutions, to execute the proposed refundings and prepayment financing as a direct purchase(s) by Barclays in one or more series; and authorize the General Manager to prepare and propose for introduction of an ordinance to be adopted by the Board of Supervisors and approved by the Mayor, authorizing the issuance of Water, Wastewater and Power bonds (or other forms of indebtedness of each enterprise, including commercial paper) to finance the respective enterprises’ shares of the costs of the 525 Golden Gate Avenue Building, as well as to refund certain BABs of the SFPUC
